data.title: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hike
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed held policy rate in 3.75%-4.00% range at October meeting
  • Inflation has been accelerating well beyond Fed's 2% target
  • A 'couple' of policymakers said half-percentage-point rate hike might be needed

By Howard Schneider

Federal Reserve officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

"Almost all" policymakers agreed that further rate hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes said, while a few said inflation could prove more persistent and require "a shift to a more restrictive policy stance" than currently expected.

"A couple" of them went further and argued that the Fed might have to resort to a half-percentage-point increase "if incoming inflation data were unfavorable," a benchmark met in recent releases that showed prices rising faster than anticipated.

Among those who supported keeping the policy rate steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range in October, "a few ... indicated that they viewed the decision as a close call," and joined a larger group in urging that the Fed be clear that "the decision to maintain the target range did not reflect a weakening" of the commitment to hit the US central bank's 2% inflation target.

At the end of the two-day session, only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of lifting the policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point.

But the debate highlighted a growing sense at the Fed that inflation will not ease enough on its own for the target to be reached quickly enough. Among those supporting a rate-hike pause, the hope is that coming information will make clearer whether inflation can fall without tighter policy.

Prices have been increasing at more than a 3% annual rate, and there has been little improvement in recent months.

Last month's meeting also set the stage for a potentially intense debate at the December 8-9 session over the need for a larger rate hike, or at least tougher language about the extent and pace of rate hikes to come, an argument laid out by Fed Governor Christopher Waller in comments to CNBC on Wednesday.

The Trump administration has argued that elevated inflation is just temporary and the Fed should ignore it.

Inflation has been stronger than expected since the Fed's last meeting, and investors anticipate that the central bank will deliver a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at its meeting next month.

The October meeting also saw the beginnings of a more detailed discussion about the impact of artificial intelligence, including discussion of the risks of over-investment in the technology as well as the possible benefits it could bring in the form of rising productivity.

data.title: Swiss Market Ends Moderately Lower
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - After opening flat and then moving slightly above the flat line till noon, the Switzerland market's benchmark SMI retreated and kept moving down till the end of the session on Wednesday.

Worries about inflation and interest rates, and falling commodity prices rendered the mood bearish.

The SMI ended the day with a loss of 89.92 points or 0.6% at 14,886.12, slightly off the day's low.

Julius Baer shed a little over 2%. Sandoz Group ended down 1.8%, while Helvetia Baloise Holding, Zurich Insurance, Novartis and UBS Group dropped 1.3%-1.6%.

Swiss Life Holding, Schindler Ps, Swiss Re, Swisscom, Geberit, Nestle, Partners Group and Kuehne + Nagel also closed weak.

Logitech International climbed nearly 3%. Richemont gained 1.45% and Sonovia avanced 1.05%. Alcon, Straumann Holding, Lonza Group, Holcim and VAT Group posted modest gains.

data.title: Spillover From Higher Energy Costs in Canada Has Been Central Bank's Main Concern — Market Talk
data.description:
1401 ET - Canada is seeing the spillover from higher energy costs spread, which was the central bank's main concern when it lifted its policy rate for the first time in more than three years, Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle says. Speaking in Alberta, Gravelle says that as the risks to inflation shifted upward policymakers felt they didn't have as much scope to provide monetary policy accommodation. The BoC has a set of models that look higher up the supply chain when energy prices are higher, and found costs of imported goods and also outside of energy are also going up. Oil price shocks are usually transitory, but the longer they stay high the less likely it is business won't pass that along, Gravelle says. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

1355 ET - Massive investment in AI is supporting the dollar, Deutsche Bank analysts say in a report as they raise their forecast for the greenback. "The AI boom has been the big factor --it has pushed US real rates higher, attracted massive equity inflows, prompted renewed inflation pressure and a hawkish Fed," they say. On balance, "the 'AI dollar' is alive and well." Deutsche Bank now expects dollar strength into 1H of 2027 with "modest weakness" in 2H. A potential headwind: a downgrade to capex expectations would undermine the dollar strength. The WSJ Dollar Index rises 0.2%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1306 ET - There's a perfect storm of three factors hitting bitcoin all at once, analysts from Yield Basis say in a research note. For one, investors now expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December, making yieldless assets more expensive to hold, they say. Secondly, there is a selloff in AI stocks that is forcing funds to decrease their risks, the analysts say. And lastly, bitcoin fell below its 200-day average, causing more than $2 billion of long positions to be forcibly closed out over the weekend, they say. On top of all that, there are concerns that AI and quantum computing could break encryption, which is tough for crypto's underdeveloped defenses, the analysts say. Bitcoin is down 1.7% at $62,830. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1207 ET - Non-U.S. buyers seem to be a key driver of recent dollar strength, Deutsche Bank's George Saravelos writes as the DXY dollar gauge hovers around a 19-month high, at 103.83. Hawkish Fedspeak also supports the currency, but Saravelos suspects it isn't enough. A Deutsche Bank tracker following more than 100 foreign-domiciled ETFs shows "extremely large dip-buying of US stocks from foreigners over the last two weeks, the largest buying spree so far this year," Saravelos says. He is skeptical that the trend will last "if market turmoil persists." (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1146 ET - Higher-taxpayers miss an opportunity in municipal bonds as they have a tendency to sell when yields rise, says Andrew Clinton of munis-focused Clinton Asset Management. Since bond prices fall when yields rise, Clinton says investors should add to their munis position when rates move upward. "There's a tendency for investors in fixed income, and munis specifically, to buy high and sell low," he says. "When the price falls, or the asset is on sale, you should be adding to it, not selling it." Clinton says demand remains high enough to absorb increasing munis supply, but it is concentrated on one- to 10-year maturities, leaving longer-dated bonds to yield beefy returns. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1136 ET - A wave of state-level tax hikes targeting high earners boosts the appeal of tax-exempt municipal bonds, says Andrew Clinton of Clinton Asset Management. He points to recent ballot measures alongside potential federal tax increases following midterm shifts and the possible expiration of current tax cuts. Clinton says investors can secure beefy returns while avoiding the volatility of equities. "Munis are one of the few asset classes where the actual value of the tax-free cash flow actually goes up should tax rates also increase," he says. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.co; @ptrevisani)

1105 ET - October home sales fell to their lowest level since 2010, in the pit of the Great Recession, Bankrate analyst Jeff Ostrowski says in a note. He points out how bizarre the current housing dynamic is compared to other parts of the economy. "If I were to say, 'Imagine a time when home prices are at record highs, the stock market has soared and the job market is near full employment,' you'd probably say, 'Wow - I bet Realtors are killing it!,'" he says. But prospective homebuyers are clearly turned off by high home prices and mortgage rates above 7%, Ostrowski says. That presents an opportunity for buyers to find a deal, so long as they can stomach the rates, he says. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1045 ET - The U.K. inflation data released on Wednesday and the jobs data released on Tuesday fail to show evidence of second-order inflation effect, reducing the prospects of the Bank of England raising rates at the Dec. 17, meeting, J.P. Morgan's Allan Monks says in a note. U.K. annual core inflation remained unchanged in October at 2.8%, below the BOE forecast of 2.9% and annual services inflation stood at 3.7%, undershooting the BOE forecast of 3.9%. The data doesn't provide a compelling reason for the BOE to raise rates rapidly, after the rate rise delivered in November, Monks says. J.P. Morgan expects a BOE rate rise in February and a potential further rate increase in the second quarter of 2027. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

1003 ET - Canadian home prices ticked higher for a third month in the last four in October, based on the latest Teranet-National Bank data. Prices rose 0.2% nationally for the month, effectively extending a period of broadly stable prices since May following a period of contraction that began in December last year. National Bank economist Daren King says the latest modest gain remains fragile, tough, with only four of the home price index's 11 markets posting increases during the month. The advance was largely supported by a 5.8% jump in Halifax, Nova Scotia. King says the plateau reached nationally masks significant disparities between markets, and the composite home price index remains 7.9% below its April 2022 peak. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)

0958 ET - Leaked documents about Deutsche Bank's operations could damage the bank's reputation but appear less likely to damage its financial position, CreditSights' Simon Adamson says in a note. Most of the revelations are based on historic events and they are already known, Adamson says. "Despite the embarrassing headlines, the consequences for Deutsche Bank look fairly limited at this stage." CreditSights maintains a "market perform" view on Deutsche Bank's additional tier 1 (AT 1) bonds, and an "outperform" view on the bank's non-preferred senior bonds. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0930 ET - Higher Swiss inflation and a weaker euro could leave the Swiss franc stronger than expected, Raiffeisen Research's Amadea Zaborszky-Hiess says in a note. Annual inflation rose to 1.5% in October from 1.0% in September, increasing the likelihood of the Swiss National Bank raising interest rates, she says. "While second-round effects remain limited for now, persistently high oil prices pose a risk of broader inflationary pressures." Raiffeisen's franc forecast was already at risk of being revised amid euro weakness on French fiscal concerns, and stronger inflationary pressures have amplified those risks, she says. For now, Raiffeisen maintains a forecast of the euro rising to 0.94 francs by year-end from 0.9246 currently before falling in the quarters ahead. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0912 ET - The euro is the weakest among the G-10 currencies, analysts at Bannockburn Capital Markets say in a note. Renewed pressure on eurozone peripheral and French bonds are helping to drag the euro lower, they say. The euro falls 0.3% to $1.0968 after reaching a 19-month low of $1.0952 earlier, according to LSEG. The 10-year German Bund yield falls 0.6 basis points to 3.382%, the 10-year French OAT yield is down 4 basis points at 4.863% and the 10-year Italian BTP yield declines 0.9 basis points to 4.428%, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Rithm Capital shares fall for seven consecutive sessions
data.description:
Rithm Capital shares fell for seven straight sessions as the stock was down 2.4% at $8.28 on Wednesday.

The alternative asset manager fell 8.5% in the preceding six sessions.

RITM is down about 23% so far this year, compared to a 7% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index (SP500).

Most recently, RITM posted stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings as net servicing revenue surged from the prior quarter.

"RITM's management is prioritizing portfolio expansion over dividend hikes or buybacks, leveraging excess EAD for growth amid a challenging macro backdrop," pointed out a recent Seeking Alpha analysis.

Looking at Wall Street community, ten analysts gave RITM a Buy and above rating. None recommended the stock hold or lower.

Seeking Alpha analysts are optimistic and see the stock as a Buy.

data.title: BellRing Brands FY 2026: Revenue $2.4B, EPS $1.25 — 10-K Summary
data.description:
BellRing Brands' revenue rose 4% while earnings fell 32% year over year, as higher volumes and Dymatize pricing lifted sales, but higher product costs, advertising and reorganization charges pressured operating profit.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent yearPrior yearYoY change
Revenue¹$2.4B$2.32B3.5%
Net income²$147.4M$216.2M(31.8%)

data.title: Nike's Investor Day Points to Long Road to Sales Recovery — Market Talk
data.description: Nike's path to recovery will require more patience from investors, Baird analysts say. At the footwear company's first investor day in years, executives said it would take 18 months or more for revenue to inflect to growth. The path to revenue growth isn't totally clear and leans on Nike's performance business, with its sportswear and China segments taking longer to improve, the analysts say. The sportswear business is expected to be pressured through fiscal 2028 while Nike tries to infuse more new models into its offerings. "Patience likely still is required until visibility to a revenue inflection becomes clearer," the analysts say.(katherine.hamilton@wsj.com)

data.title: Ewing Morris Announces Successful Completion of Its Offer for Shares of Decibel Cannabis Company Inc.
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Ewing Morris, on behalf of investment vehicles and accounts managed by it ("Ewing Morris"), today announced the completion of its all-cash offer (the "Offer") to acquire common shares (the "Shares") in the capital of Decibel Cannabis Company Inc. (OTCQB: DBCCF) ("Decibel") at a price of $2.09 per Share, for an aggregate cost of approximately $4,661,113.82.

In connection with the completion of the Offer, Ewing Morris will take up and pay for Shares that have been validly tendered and not withdrawn within three (3) business days. Following the take-up and payment for such Shares, Ewing Morris will own a total of 2,230,198 Shares, representing approximately 5.79% of Decibel's issued and outstanding Shares.

Payment for the purchased Shares will be effected by Odyssey Trust Company, the depository for the Offer, in accordance with the Offer and applicable law. Shareholders of Decibel who have validly deposited and not withdrawn their Shares are not required to take any further action to accept the Offer.

The investment reflects Ewing Morris's broader strategy of bringing a private-equity mindset to the public markets-emphasizing active engagement, alignment of interests, and sustainable long-term value creation.

data.title: U.S. indexes are mixed after Nvidia earnings; gold declines
data.description:
Wall Street's major averages were mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia (NVDA) reported better-than-expected Q3 results amid the recent CEO scandal. Investor sentiment was shaken as they now turn to upcoming FOMC minutes from the last meeting.

The benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.4%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was flat, and the blue-chip Dow was -1.1%.

Nvidia shares seesawed and were last -2.2% after the company reported Q3 results that showed a 75% year-over-year revenue growth estimate for the fiscal year ending January 2028.

“Nvidia earnings are a tech bellwether in the same way that GDP tells you what the economy was doing three months ago,” said Dario Perkins, managing director of Global Macro at TS Lombard.

“Technology is down to 35.4% of the S&P 500 and more than 19% off the recent highs. Still outperforming the S&P 500 YTD though,” Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, added.

On the economic side, U.S. housing starts jumped 9.9% month-over-month in October, more than expected, while permits increased less than consensus anticipated. In addition, the October U.S. Pending Home Sales Index slid -4.7% this month, more than expected.

Later today, the Federal Reserve will release the minutes from its last meeting. Bank of America expects the minutes to reveal a deeper divide over the decision to be on rate hold than the 10-2 vote suggested.

The gold spot price is down 2.8% on Wednesday due to hawkish monetary policy expectations and the ongoing stock market weakness.

Over to the bond market, yields were lower. The 10-year Treasury yield () declined 5 basis points to 5.07%, while the 2-year Treasury yield () also was 3 basis points lower at 4.79%. The 30-year Treasury yield was 4 basis points lower at 5.42%.

Oil prices were mostly lower. Crude oil futures were $84, while Brent was $91 per barrel.

data.title: Google expands Project Genie with real-time editing of AI-generated worlds
data.description:
Google is expanding access to Project Genie, an experimental AI tool that lets users create and explore interactive virtual worlds, adding real-time editing, audio, and longer exploration sessions.

The updated experience will be available to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, the company said Thursday.

The company said the technology remains experimental. "We are actively tackling key challenges such as camera latency, intricate physical interactions, real-time audio precision, and long-term scene permanence," Google said in its blogpost.

The update introduces access to Genie 4, Google's latest world model, which allows users to modify environments through text prompts while exploring them. Users can change weather conditions, add characters, or alter events as they move through a generated world. The model also generates audio, including background sounds and character dialogue, that changes with the scene.

Google is also extending the capabilities of Genie 3, allowing users to explore generated worlds for up to three minutes per session, compared with 60 seconds previously. Users can also link multiple worlds together and create environments using 360-degree panoramic images.

Google said generated video and audio include SynthID watermarks and that inputs and outputs are screened for safety.

data.title: Ondo to launch tokenized Anthropic stock on IPO day
data.description:
Ondo Finance, a crypto company that tokenizes stocks and other assets, plans to launch a token tied to Anthropic shares on Thursday, when the AI company is slated to start trading on Nasdaq.

The token is called ANTon and will be available to eligible investors outside the U.S., according to a Wednesday release.

Anthropic is expected to set its final IPO price after market close on Wednesday before shares debut under the ticker ANT.

The public offering could become the largest in history, with analysts projecting the debut to bring in around $90 billion at the top end of its range. This would edge out the $85.7 billion raised by SpaceX in its record IPO in June.

"ANTon is live on IPO day, it mints and redeems after New York goes home, and it works like other assets onchain," said Ian De Bode, Ondo Finance’s president and acting CEO.

Ondo affirmed that minting and redemption will run 24/7 and said it will waive minting fees and charge a reduced redemption fee. Ondo did not say how long this would apply. The Block reached out to Ondo for clarification.

ANTon gives holders exposure to ANT share prices, but holders will not have direct ownership of the stock. It will join more than 450 other tokenized stocks and ETFs on Ondo Stocks, which the company says has passed $1 billion in total value locked.

data.title: BIDU Stock Slumps To Fresh 16 Year Low, BABA Shares Down To New 22-Month Low – Here’s What Investors Are Watching
data.description:
Key points:
  • Susquehanna slashed BIDU’s target to $75 from $105, and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating, according to The Fly.
  • Alibaba is scheduled to report its September-quarter results on Thursday.
  • Alibaba is facing scrutiny, with the Trump administration reportedly considering requiring U.S. companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models.

Chinese firms Baidu (BIDU) and Alibaba (BABA) faced fresh headwinds on Wednesday, as Wall Street lowered Baidu’s price targets after its quarterly earnings, while Alibaba came under renewed scrutiny over its AI business and reported links to the Nvidia (NVDA) controversy.

At the time of writing, BIDU shares were down 1.7% to their lowest levels since July 2010, while BABA stock fell around 1% to levels last seen in January 2025.

Baidu Sees Price Target Cuts Due To Weak Advertising Business

Wall Street continued to lower BIDU’s price target on Wednesday, with Susquehanna slashing its target by more than 28% following its third-quarter (Q3) earnings.

The brokerage cut BIDU’s target to $75 from $105, and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating, according to The Fly. Susquehanna said that while Baidu’s General Business returned to growth, driven by stronger AI Cloud Infrastructure performance, continued weakness in its legacy online advertising business is holding back the overall recovery.

Barclays also lowered its target on BIDU to $72 from $80, while keeping an ‘Equal Weight’ rating.

On Monday, Baidu reported a 1% decline in Q3 revenue to $4.6 billion, while adjusted earnings per American depositary share (ADS) fell to $1.01 from $1.66 a year earlier. However, both figures beat analysts’ expectations, according to Fiscal.ai.

Online advertising revenue dropped 22% to RMB11.9 billion ($1.77 billion), while AI Cloud Infrastructure revenue surged 94% to RMB8.2 billion.

Retail sentiment surrounding BIDU on Stocktwits turned ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes. BIDU shares are down over 53% so far in 2026.

Alibaba’s Qwen Faces Potential U.S. Scrutiny

Alibaba Group (BABA) is facing scrutiny over its AI business, with the Trump administration reportedly considering requiring U.S. companies to disclose their use of Chinese AI models.

The proposal could affect American businesses using Alibaba’s Qwen AI models, including Airbnb. However, no formal regulation has been announced.

On Tuesday, The Information report tied Alibaba to suspected spy Alice Huang and her firm, Megaspeed. Nvidia reportedly introduced Alibaba to Alice Huang in 2022, helping her firm Megaspeed secure Alibaba as a customer.

At the time of writing, the firm had not responded to Stocktwits’ request for comments on the reports.

Alibaba is also scheduled to report September-quarter results on Thursday. According to Fiscal AI, Wall Street estimates an 11% year-over-year revenue increase to RMB 269.60 billion, with earnings expected to rise to RMB 11.03 per share from RMB 4.59 per share.

Retail sentiment surrounding BABA on Stocktwits remained ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, amid ‘extremely high’ message volumes. BIDU shares are down over 45% so far in 2026.

data.title: 5 AI Stocks That Could Win After Huang’s Nvidia Exit
data.description:
After 33 years running NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA), Jensen Huang has stepped down. For the companies that have spent years trying to win business away from Nvidia, his exit may be the opening they’ve been waiting for.

Luke Lango put it bluntly on the November 17 episode of The Investor Place: “Without that leather shield, I think those efforts can make a lot more headway.”

The “leather shield” is Huang himself. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD), Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) and Google parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) have all built alternatives to Nvidia’s chips, yet Luke argues Huang’s charisma at the negotiating table was one of the reasons the biggest buyers kept coming back. With CFO Colette Kress now serving as interim CEO, he thinks those buyers will start taking a harder look at their options.

Luke, Louis Navellier and Eric Fry each see a different way to play it. Luke named five stocks he thinks could benefit. Louis is holding on to Nvidia. And Eric is focused on the companies putting AI to work.

Editor’s note: This episode was recorded before Nvidia reported its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on November 17, 2026. Comments about the upcoming report reflect the panelists’ expectations at the time of filming.

What Huang’s Exit Means for Nvidia and the AI Trade

All three panelists expect Nvidia’s near-term business to hold up. “The 2027 road map is locked in,” Luke said. “Nothing’s going to change in the 2027 numbers.” Louis was even more direct: “We got four years of orders.” Even Eric, the most cautious of the three, said 2027 demand is “baked into the cake.”

The uncertainty starts in 2028. That’s when big customers make their next round of purchasing decisions, and Luke believes rivals will push harder without Huang across the table. Louis pointed to the advantage Nvidia keeps regardless of who runs it: CUDA, the software developers have spent years writing for Nvidia’s chips. Replacing the hardware means replacing that software too, and no competitor offers an equal substitute yet.

Eric is more worried about money than chips. Nvidia has lent heavily to its own customers, and he noted reporting that Kress has been less enthusiastic than Huang about extending that credit. “Nvidia has been called the central bank of AI, right? Because of its ability to finance its own customers,” Eric said. If that support pulls back, he sees it as “very, very negative for the ecosystem broadly.”

The panel saw the market’s reaction as a sign investors share that worry. On the day Huang left, CoreWeave, Inc. (CRWV), Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) and Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL) all fell further than Nvidia did.

Nvidia’s first report without Huang came out after filming. The company posted fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year earlier, and guided to about $130 billion for the fourth quarter, plus or minus 3% (Nvidia, November 17, 2026).

Luke Lango’s 5 AI Stocks to Watch Beyond Nvidia

Luke’s case comes down to market share. By his estimate, Nvidia controls roughly 85% of the AI chip market today and builds much of the surrounding data center gear, like networking and optics, in-house. If that share slips to “let’s say, mid-60s,” he said, “that 20 points translates downstream through the whole chain.”

That’s why the stocks that rallied the day Huang left went well beyond AMD. Luke is bullish on three chipmakers and sees two more opportunities in networking and data center hardware. Here they are, starting with his favorite.

Broadcom: Luke’s Top Pick

Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) designs custom AI chips for the biggest cloud companies. Luke said he’s bullish on all three chipmakers, but Broadcom stands out because “the custom silicon projects are the ones that are going to accelerate the most as a result of the Nvidia situation.”

He also likes how Broadcom holds up if AI spending cools. Luke listed several pressures on 2027 and 2028 budgets: widening debt spreads, a rising 10-year Treasury yield, supply shortages and political pushback against data center construction. If the big spenders pull back, he expects them to lean harder on their own chip programs, which is exactly where Broadcom works. In his words, “Broadcom’s actually in a pretty good position regardless of which way the wind blows in ’27.”

Advanced Micro Devices: The Headline Challenger

Luke called AMD the “headline winner” if Nvidia loses ground. He credited CEO Lisa Su with “a really good product roadmap” and pointed to AMD’s recent deals with Anthropic and Amazon.

He admits AMD is still behind. Every competitor is. But Huang’s exit gives buyers a reason to rethink their 2028 plans, and Luke thinks Su now carries more weight in negotiations than whoever Nvidia puts in front of customers.

Marvell Technology: Another Custom Silicon Play

Marvell Technology, Inc. (MRVL) works with large customers on custom chips, much like Broadcom. Luke grouped it with Broadcom as a custom silicon partner that rallied the day Huang was pushed out, and he’s bullish on it, though Broadcom remains his preferred way to play the trend.

Arista Networks: A Networking Opening

Arista Networks, Inc. (ANET) sells the networking equipment that connects servers in large data centers. Customers who buy Nvidia’s systems often take Nvidia’s networking along with them. If they shift some purchases elsewhere, Luke expects more of that business to go to “non-Nvidia networking,” which is Arista’s specialty.

Celestica: Strong Backlog, Weak Grade

Celestica Inc. (CLS) builds data center hardware, and Luke counted it among the stocks that did well the day Huang left. “Celestica’s in that game,” he said.

Louis owns it, though with a caveat. Celestica “slipped to a D-rating in Stock Grader,” he said, “but the fundamentals were so good and the backlog was so good, we held it and we’re happy to see it’s now rallying.” He hopes to see the grade climb to a C soon.

Luke tracks the companies positioned to profit from shifts like this one, from custom chips to data center infrastructure. To get his latest research, sign up for his free Hypergrowth Investing e-letter.

Louis Navellier Is Still Holding Nvidia Stock

Nvidia is “our largest holding actually in terms of what we own,” Louis said. Part of the reason is that the position grew so much and he didn’t want to pay the taxes on selling it. But he also likes what he sees. Louis cited margins near 70%, a growing order backlog and what he called a low price-to-earnings ratio. He called it “a very safe hold here near term.”

He’s clear about what would change his mind. Louis said three things would be warning signs: analysts cutting earnings estimates, margins coming under pressure or the order backlog peaking.

For the panel’s first reactions to the shakeup, see our earlier coverage of Huang’s departure.

Louis uses his quantitative system to separate stocks with strong fundamentals from the ones just riding headlines. For his market outlook and stock analysis, sign up for his free Market 360 e-letter.

Eric Fry Is Looking Beyond the AI Builders

Eric sees the AI trade “widening out” rather than breaking down. He has been looking to pivot from companies that build AI, like Nvidia, toward companies that use it. He admits the market hasn’t rewarded that shift yet: the two groups have performed about the same. And he’s not telling anyone to dump the builders. “You can still own a lot of builders,” he said.

Still, Huang’s exit doesn’t change where he’s hunting. “I’m not looking for opportunity close to that epicenter,” Eric said. His focus is biopharma and medical technology. “I’m going to just keep banging that drum because I think that’s the best, most exciting area to be looking.”

Eric’s research focuses on spotting major investment trends before the crowd does. For his latest ideas, sign up for his free Smart Money e-letter.

What Investors Should Watch Next

The biggest open question is who runs Nvidia next. Luke thinks the most likely candidate is Rene Haas, CEO of Arm Holdings plc (ARM), who spent seven years at Nvidia, and he called that “a hire that would really help the stock.” Some analysts argue Nvidia is worth 25% less without Huang. Luke said that could prove true if the new CEO can’t protect Nvidia’s position in 2028 and beyond.

After that, watch where customers spend. If the big cloud companies keep committing to Nvidia, its lead likely holds. If more of their budgets go to custom chips and outside networking, Luke’s five stocks could benefit. And if Nvidia gets stingier with customer financing, Eric’s concern about the broader AI ecosystem moves to the front.

Get More Free Investing Research

As Nvidia adjusts to life after Jensen Huang, stay ahead of the AI trade with free research from all three InvestorPlace experts.

Louis Navellier | Market 360: Get Louis’s daily market commentary and earnings-driven stock picks. Join Market 360 for free.

Luke Lango | Hypergrowth Investing: Follow the AI and emerging tech companies Luke thinks are built for long-term growth. Start reading Hypergrowth Investing.

Eric Fry | Smart Money: See the major economic trends Eric is tracking, plus the market risks he’s watching. Get Smart Money free.

Frequently Asked Questions About AI Stocks After Jensen Huang

Which AI stock does Luke Lango like most after Jensen Huang’s exit?

Broadcom. Luke is also bullish on AMD and Marvell, but he believes Broadcom’s custom chip business stands to gain the most and holds up best if AI spending slows.

Could AMD take market share from Nvidia?

Luke thinks so, mainly from 2028 on. AMD has a strong product roadmap and recent deals with Anthropic and Amazon. Nvidia’s CUDA software remains a major hurdle for any competitor.

Is Louis Navellier selling Nvidia stock?

No. Louis said Nvidia is the largest holding in what his team owns. He plans to keep it unless analysts cut estimates, margins shrink or the order backlog peaks.

data.title: Fed's Barr Expects Further Rate Increases Will Be Appropriate
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

Federal Reserve governor Michael Barr said he believes it will be appropriate to raise rates further to achieve the central bank's 2% goal.

"Inflation is too high, making it hard for American families to make ends meet," according Barr's remarks set to be delivered in New York on Wednesday.

"If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further to achieve that goal," according to Barr.

Recent comments among officials this week solidify the commitment for policymakers to combat inflation, but the question is how quickly they should move. The Fed held interest rates steady last month, and the next interest-rate decision will take place on Dec. 9.

This morning, Fed governor Christopher Waller explained the central bank may need to "shock people" to help them understand inflation should be under 3%.

"People are starting to think 3% may be the norm," Waller said Wednesday on CNBC. "That's the kind of psychology I think we need to start breaking," he added.

On Tuesday, New York Fed President John Williams said the current inflation situation doesn't call for "dramatic action," but reiterated his view there is still work to do to get inflation back down to 2%.

Write to Jessica Coacci at jessica.coacci@wsj.com

data.title: Europe’s clean-energy push deepens dependence on Chinese technology
data.description:
Europe’s transition away from imported fossil fuels is creating a different overseas dependence: Chinese clean-energy equipment. Wind and solar generated more EU electricity than fossil fuels last year, but inexpensive Chinese technology is helping drive that expansion while squeezing European manufacturers, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

For investors, Europe’s response could reshape competition across solar, batteries and wind power. Procurement preferences and subsidies may support domestic suppliers, while restrictions on cheaper imports could raise developers’ costs and slow installations. Policy decisions will help determine which businesses capture the transition’s growth.

China produces at least 80% of the world’s solar products and lithium-ion batteries. European wind-turbine manufacturers retain a stronger position, although they rely heavily on Chinese rare-earth magnets.

The EU has proposed favoring European-made solar panels, turbines and batteries in public contracts. Some governments also subsidize purchases of locally manufactured equipment, but substantial price differences make it difficult to change buying habits.

Chinese wind equipment costs 30% to 45% less to manufacture, while Chinese electrolyzers used to produce hydrogen can cost less than half their European equivalents. Protecting domestic production could therefore make Europe’s climate goals more expensive to achieve.

Security concerns are adding pressure for restrictions. The EU has barred Chinese inverters from EU-funded projects and is considering broader limits. These devices connect solar generation to usable electricity, and experts warn coordinated cyberattacks could disrupt power supplies.

Europe’s challenge is deciding which industries warrant support. Bruegel researcher Simone Tagliapietra argues that inexpensive solar imports have accelerated deployment and created installation jobs, while Europe could concentrate industrial investment in stronger businesses such as cables and wind turbines.

data.title: Skydance is combining the Warner Bros. and Paramount TV studios
data.description:
Skydance Corporation is already making major post-merger moves. The media giant announced that it will combine Warner Bros. Television and Paramount Television Studios into a single TV studio entity that will have more than 100 productions under its control. The new organization will be called Warner Bros. Television Studios and will launch early next year.

The merged studio unit is being co-led by Channing Dungey (head of Warner Bros. Television Group) and Matt Thunell (president of Paramount Television Studios). Both will report to George Cheeks, who oversees Skydance's broader television operations.

As part of the same broader TV restructuring, Skydance has also folded its television animation assets (Warner Bros. Animation, Cartoon Network Studios, Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe, and Nickelodeon Animation Studios) into a single division called Skydance Television Animation.

The consolidation is a major piece of Skydance's post-merger integration strategy aimed at achieving $6B in annual synergies within three years. Separately, Skydance is considering combining Paramount+ and HBO Max into one streaming service.

Shares of Skydance are up about 2% since the mega-merger closed.
